name: Lyman E. Johnson
role: Early missionary and member of the first Twelve
dateNote: He was baptized in February 1831, became an apostle in 1835, and was excommunicated on 13 April 1838.
importance: Section 68 answers his request, with three other elders, to know the Lord’s will in November 1831. Section 75 sends him east with Orson Pratt. He was one of the original Twelve Apostles in 1835. He was excommunicated in April 1838, and section 118 fills the vacancies left in the Twelve.
connections: He was a son of John and Elsa Johnson of Hiram, Ohio, and a brother of Luke Johnson. His companions in these sections were Orson Pratt, Orson Hyde, and William E. McLellin.

sources.title: Lyman Eugene Johnson, Joseph Smith Papers biography

reviewNote: JSP: born 24 Oct. 1811, Pomfret, Vermont; baptized Feb. 1831 by Sidney Rigdon; high priest 2 Nov. 1831; apostle 1835–1838; excommunicated 13 Apr. 1838; drowned 20 Dec. 1859 near Prairie du Chien, Wisconsin. Bare “Lyman” left out (it also names Lyman Wight and Lyman Sherman).
